first.rationale: Two structural declines (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%) are internally controllable and have strong prior evidence (memory_31, memory_86) of durable improvement from signup simplification and activation messaging. Promotional pricing (memory_73) is tempting given the competitor's price move on SMB, but reactive price-matching risks attracting low-quality, price-sensitive accounts and eroding margin/retention in a way that conflicts with 'sustainable long-term qualified revenue' — this needs verification of the original record before ever committing spend, especially the claim it held across both billing plans, since that's the kind of durable-sounding generalization that most often gets overstated on reconsolidation. I also want to verify memory_31 because it's the oldest, most-consolidated memory touching the exact metric now regressing (onboarding completion), and I want to confirm the original effect size and population before betting this week's single experiment slot on it. Given only one experiment slot, fixing the internally-caused onboarding regression is the more defensible, less speculative bet than entering a pricing war reactively; I'm running it as a standard (not broad) experiment to preserve ability to course-correct, and explicitly flagging that the competitive pricing pressure remains unaddressed and may need its own future experiment once verified.
